Subject: Three things to do on the trail this autumn
CTA: Share this with your trail crew -> https://www.example.com/trail-care-newsletter
Body: Autumn is the season that shows you where you cut corners in the spring. Here are three trail-care habits worth building before the ground freezes.

**1. Clear drainage before the rain really arrives.**
Water is the primary driver of trail erosion. Walk your regular routes now and clear any debris — leaves, sticks, accumulated duff — from drainage dips, rolling grade dips, and outsloped sections. A few minutes of raking before a heavy rain can prevent months of rut repair. Target anything that forces water to run down the tread rather than off it.

**2. Fill and tamp soft spots while the soil still has moisture.**
A soft spot in October is a hole in April. While the ground holds enough moisture to compact, fill low sections with native mineral soil and tamp in layers of roughly 3 to 4 inches at a time. Avoid organic fill — it breaks down and leaves you with the same depression next year.

**3. Mark your problem areas before snow covers them.**
Place small cairns, flagging, or stakes at spots that need attention in spring — undermined roots, failing retaining structures, sections that ice early. Memory is unreliable over a winter. A simple sketch or phone note with GPS coordinates costs nothing and saves a full scouting trip in March.

These are small acts. They add up across a season and across a community of people who use the same trails.
